title: Understanding Gradient Descent
text: Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm used to minimize a function by iteratively moving towards the steepest descent, as defined by the negative of the gradient. Can you think of why it might work with both convex and non-convex functions?

title: Convex vs Non-Convex Functions
text: Convex functions have a single global minimum, while non-convex functions can have multiple local minima. How might this affect the path gradient descent takes?

title: Gradient Descent and Function Types
text: Which of the following statements is true about gradient descent?
choices: Gradient descent can work with both convex and $$non-convex$$ functions.
Gradient descent is not suitable for optimization problems.
Gradient descent is only applicable to linear functions.
Gradient descent only works with convex functions.
